# BPMN Process Modelling

BPMN 2.0 (OMG Business Process Model and Notation — **not** UML) models the work that happens
*around* a system rather than inside it: who does what, in which order, who waits on whom, and what
happens when a step fails. A model is a **collaboration** when it spans more than one participant:
each participant is a *pool*, roles inside a pool are *lanes*, sequence flows may not leave a pool,
and anything crossing a pool boundary must be a *message flow*.

`Information-Systems-Modelling` lab 7 ships **8 collaborations** covering the ModellingClub
platform's operational life cycle. This is the only place in the source set where formal process
models exist as real artefacts rather than as prose.

## The eight processes

| # | Process | Theme | Notation exercised |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Scheduled Backup & Verification | maintenance | timer start, parallel split/join, boundary error, error end |
| 2 | Software Upgrade / Dependency Patch | maintenance | message start, severity gateway, staging loop-back, rollback |
| 3 | Release & Blue-Green Deployment | deployment | parallel build+test, approval gate, 5 lanes |
| 4 | H2 → PostgreSQL Migration | deployment | maintenance-window timer, reversible cut-over |
| 5 | Data Archiving, Retention & GDPR Erasure | data / security | two start events, legal-hold gateway, 30-day boundary timer |
| 6 | Security Incident Response | data / security | signal start, 3-way severity, 72 h GDPR timer |
| 7 | Member Onboarding & Provisioning | business | 3-pool collaboration, boundary timer, SLA accept/reject |
| 8 | System Decommissioning / End-of-Life | business | notice timers, **terminate end**, contract-termination message flow |

Participants reach well beyond the application's own actors — DevOps, Release Manager, DBA, Data
Protection Officer, security on-call, an Operations Committee, the cloud provider, offsite storage
and the GDPR supervisory authority. Several are modelled as **black-box pools**: present, addressed
by message flow, with no internal detail. That is the correct BPMN treatment of a party whose
internals you do not control.

Process 4 is a quiet cross-reference: the thing being migrated is [[h2-database]], the actual dev
database of labs 3 and 4.

## Three artefacts from one specification

Each process exists once, as a JavaScript object in `lab7/src/specs.js` (605 lines), declaring pools,
lanes, nodes with event markers, sequence flows and message flows. A ~1,400-line zero-dependency Node
generator turns that into three deliverables: a self-contained **SVG** diagram, a Camunda-compatible
**`.bpmn` XML file including diagram interchange (DI)**, and a section of the PDF report. See
[[single-source-of-truth-generators]] and [[generate-markup-instead-of-hand-writing-it]].

Diagram interchange matters here: a `.bpmn` file without DI carries the semantics but not the
layout, so a modeller re-opening it gets a valid process arranged as a heap. `lab7/src/layout.js`
(307 lines) computes a layered auto-layout so that the SVG a reader sees and the `.bpmn` a modeller
opens show the same picture.

Files are numbered `p1-backup` … `p8-eol` across `bpmn/`, `diagrams/` and the `P1`…`P8` constants in
`specs.js` — see [[numbered-stages-in-directory-names]].

## What was checked, and what could not be

> "Every model was checked against BPMN execution semantics: each path reaches an end event;
> parallel splits are matched by parallel joins; exclusive / event-based gateways carry
> mutually-exclusive conditions; message flows only ever cross a pool boundary."
> — Information-Systems-Modelling/lab7/README.md, 2026-07-09

That is a real correctness checklist, and it is the right one. But the same README also asserts all
eight files import warning-free in `bpmn-moddle`, and **`bpmn-moddle` appears in no `package.json`
and no script anywhere in the repo**.
